bib.title: A weakly informative default prior distribution for logistic and other regression models

question: What default prior on coefficients of classical logistic regression gives stable, regularized estimates (including under separation) while remaining weak enough for routine automatic use?
hypothesis: Real logistic coefficients on standardized inputs are rarely larger than 5, so independent Student-t/Cauchy priors on them should beat maximum likelihood and competing priors predictively and stabilise separated fits.
contributions: Prior: scale non-binary inputs to mean 0 and sd 0.5, then independent Student-t priors; default Cauchy centre 0 scale 2.5 (10 for the intercept)
bayesglm: approximate EM inside iteratively weighted least squares, implemented in R's arm package
Three applications: vote-preference regressions, bioassay, chained-imputation of HIV viral load
Five-fold cross-validation over 45 UCI datasets comparing priors, glm, Jeffreys (brglm) and BBR

method.summary: Inputs are standardized (binary centred, others sd 0.5) and each coefficient gets an independent Cauchy(0, 2.5) prior (Cauchy(0,10) for the constant). The posterior mode is found by adding J pseudo-data points to the weighted least squares step of IRLS and updating prior scales by an approximate EM step (t as normal scale mixture). Priors are compared by five-fold cross-validated log and Brier score on 45 UCI datasets.
method.task: regularised logistic regression / default prior choice

datasets.name: UCI Machine Learning Repository corpus (45 datasets, Fig 5)
datasets.source: UCI repository (Newman et al 1998; Asuncion and Newman 2007); datasets with continuous outcome or logical-theory form excluded
datasets.preprocessing: Missingness is a separate indicator predictor per variable with missing values; continuous predictors discretised by Fayyad and Irani (1993); k-level predictor becomes k-1 binary predictors (most frequent level dropped); multinomial outcomes become most-frequent category vs the rest

datasets.split: separate logistic regression per election year
datasets.preprocessing: binary inputs female and black centred; income (1-5 scale) centred and divided by two standard deviations

models.name: bayesglm (Cauchy/t prior, approximate EM-IRLS posterior mode)
models.architecture: logistic regression with independent t priors
models.init_from: beta = 0 or a guess (e.g. unit normal draws); each sigma_j initialised to s_j

other.default_prior: Cauchy (nu=1), centre 0, scale 10 for intercept, 2.5 for binary predictors, 2.5/(2*sd) for other numeric predictors
other.t_family: nu and scale s varied in the cross-validation; nu=1 Cauchy, nu=inf Gaussian

other.note: under no finite MLE defined as R default starting value and default iterations

models.name: brglm (Kosmidis 2007)
models.architecture: Jeffreys prior bias reduction, logit and probit links

models.name: BBR (Genkin, Lewis, Madigan 2007)
models.architecture: Bayesian binary regression with Laplace (l) or Gaussian (g) prior

other.scale_heuristic: k / E[x.x], k = dimensions of x; averaged about 2.0 across the datasets

training.objective: posterior mode of logistic likelihood with independent t priors (approximate EM: IRLS step then E and M steps)
training.optimizer: iteratively weighted least squares with pseudo-data for the prior plus approximate EM update of prior scales (sigma_j^2 = ((beta_j-mu_j)^2 + V_jj + nu_j s_j^2)/(1+nu_j))

other.convergence: 'until approximate convergence'; no tolerance or iteration count given
other.covariance: inverse second derivative of log-posterior at the estimate
other.other_models: linear regression: rescale outcome to mean 0 sd 0.5 (or multiply prior scale by sd of y), add a step for data variance

inference.samples: five random 5-fold partitions per dataset is not stated; one five-fold CV per dataset and prior setting is implied

parameters.input_scaling: binary mean 0 diff 1; others mean 0 sd 0.5

metrics.name: logarithmic score
metrics.definition: -log p_y where p_y is the cross-validated predicted probability of the true outcome, averaged over datasets

metrics.name: Brier score
metrics.definition: (1 - p_y)^2 / 2 as printed, averaged over datasets

baselines: brglm Jeffreys prior, logit and probit
bayesglm with Gaussian and t_nu priors at varied scales
eval.protocol: Five-fold cross-validation; posterior mode fitted on training folds, predicted probabilities on test fold; mean log and Brier loss averaged over the 45 datasets. No significance tests or seeds reported.

limits: Prior depends on the data through standardization, so it changes as data arrive; authors concede trouble with very small samples (Section 6).
Evaluates the posterior mode, not full posterior simulation (Section 5.1).
Always returning an estimate can mask nonidentifiability; authors reply that ML can also be fit.
CV optimum (Cauchy 0.75) differs from the recommended 2.5, and best prior varies by dataset.
Corpus is 45 UCI datasets with mostly binary predictors; no seeds, repeated CV, or significance tests; convergence criteria not stated.
Multinomial logit and probit not handled; fully Bayesian hierarchical version left as an extension.
Later work (Stan prior-choice guidance) may have superseded the 2.5 scale default; not in this paper.
